newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Suharto to visit Burma, Cambodia, Laos.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Suharto to visit Burma, Cambodia, Laos.

text.p: Indonesia's President Suharto will visit Burma next week, just days after of a meeting of European and Southeast Asian nations at which Rangoon's military rulers came under heavy fire.
State Secretary Murdiono said Suharto would make state visits to Cambodia from February 17 to 19, Laos from February 19 to 21 and Burma between February 21 and 23.
Leaders of all three countries had recently visited Indonesia, he said.
Suharto is due to have talks with the head of the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) in Burma.

The issue of Burma and Indonesia's record in the former Portuguese colony of East Timor had threatened to derail the meeting between the European Union and the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) in Singapore this week.
But delegates in Singapore said on Thursday the two blocs were set to agree on a plan to broaden ties, despite human rights differences.
ASEAN members Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei, Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam have rebuffed Western protests over the grouping's relations with Burma.
The other ASEAN states have also firmly aligned themselves behind Indonesia against Portugal's efforts to isolate Jakarta over its rights record in disputed East Timor.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 after a civil war followed Portugal's abrupt decolonisation of the territory. Up to a third of the population died in the famine and fighting that followed.
Indonesia then annexed East Timor in 1976, but the United Nations still considers Portugal the administering power.
Burma, Cambodia and Laos are also due to join ASEAN, possibly later this year.
Diplomats said the major significance of Suharto's tour was that he was visiting prospective members of the group, whose founders envisaged a community embracing all 10 Southeast Asian nations.
Suharto last visited Burma in 1974 when General Ne Win was formally in power, and he will be the first senior statesman to visit the country in several years.
"The leaders will make the best possible use of the visits to improve bilateral relations, and in particular to expand economic and trade cooperation," Murdiono said.

"In Cambodia, President Suharto will witness the signing of a memorandum of understanding (MOU) in the oil and gas sector," he said. Suharto last visited Cambodia in 1968 before the war in Vietnam spilled over and engulfed the small nation.
Indonesia's state oil company Pertamina has said it will participate in Cambodia's oil industry.
In Laos, Suharto was expected to witness the signing of an MOU covering the agricultural and forestry sectors.
